summary: Beis Shammai say that for most korbanos one putting of blood on the mizbeach is enough, but a chatas needs two; Beis Hillel say even a chatas needs only one. So only the first putting decides whether a korban becomes piggul.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

words.note: Beis Shammai, the students of Shammai.

chunks.en: all blood that is put on the outer mizbeach,
chunks.st: With regard to all the offerings whose blood is to be placed on the external altar,
chunks.stMore: even those that require that the blood be sprinkled on two opposite corners of the altar so that it will run down each of its four sides,

words.note: The big mizbeach in the courtyard.

chunks.en: if he put it with only one putting,
chunks.st: in a case where the priest placed the blood on the altar with only one placement,

chunks.en: it brought kapparah. And for a chatas,
chunks.st: he facilitated atonement. And in the case of a sin offering,
chunks.stMore: which requires four placements, one on each of the four corners of the altar,

words.note: Forgiveness; the korban did its job.

chunks.en: two puttings are needed.
chunks.st: at least two placements are necessary to facilitate atonement.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: even a chatas that he put with one putting
chunks.st: Even with regard to a sin offering, in a case where the priest placed the blood with one placement,

chunks.en: brought kapparah. Therefore,
chunks.st: he facilitated atonement after the fact. Therefore,
chunks.stMore: since the priest facilitates atonement with one placement in all cases other than a sin offering according to Beit Shammai, and even in the case of a sin offering according to Beit Hillel,

chunks.en: if he put the first one the right way,
chunks.st: if he placed the first placement in its proper manner,

chunks.en: and the second planning for after its time,
chunks.st: and the second with the intent to eat the offering beyond its designated time,

chunks.he: כִּפֵּר. נָתַן אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה חוּץ לִזְמַנָּהּ
chunks.en: it brought kapparah. If he put the first planning for after its time,
chunks.st: he facilitated atonement. Since the second placement is not indispensable with regard to achieving atonement, improper intent while performing that rite does not invalidate the offering. And based on the same reasoning, if he placed the first placement with the intent to eat the offering beyond its designated time

chunks.en: and the second planning for outside its place,
chunks.st: and he placed the second placement with the intent to eat the offering outside its designated area, the second of which does not render an offering piggul,

chunks.en: it is piggul, and one who eats it gets kares.
chunks.st: the offering is piggul, an offering disqualified by improper intention, and one is liable to receive excision from the World-to-Come [karet] for its
chunks.stMore: consumption. This is because the intent that accompanied the second placement does not supersede the piggul status of the offering.

summary: Blood that is put on the inner, golden mizbeach must be put every single time. If even one putting was done with a wrong thought, the korban is pasul, but it is not piggul.
stIntro: All this applies to those offerings whose blood is to be placed on the external altar.

chunks.en: All blood that is put on the inner mizbeach,
chunks.st: But with regard to all the offerings whose blood is to be placed on the inner altar,

words.note: The golden mizbeach inside the Heichal.

chunks.en: if he left out even one of the puttings,
chunks.st: if the priest omitted even one of the placements,

chunks.en: it did not bring kapparah.
chunks.st: it is as though he did not facilitate atonement.

chunks.en: Therefore, if he put all of them the right way,
chunks.st: Therefore, if he placed all the placements in their proper manner,

chunks.en: and one not the right way,
chunks.st: and one placement in an improper manner,
chunks.stMore: i.e., with the intent to eat the offering beyond its designated time,

chunks.en: it is pasul, but there is no kares.
chunks.st: the offering is disqualified, as it is lacking one placement; but there is no liability for karet for
chunks.stMore: one who partakes of the offering, as the improper intention related to only part of the blood that renders the offering permitted for consumption, and an offering becomes piggul only when the improper intention relates to the entire portion of the offering that renders it permitted for consumption.

summary: Some things cannot become piggul, because nothing else makes them allowed, like the kometz, the ketores and the blood. Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Meir argue about the metzora's log of oil.

chunks.en: These are things for which one is not punished
chunks.st: And these are the items for which one is not liable

chunks.en: because of piggul:
chunks.st: to receive karet due to violation of the prohibition of piggul.
chunks.stMore: One is liable to receive karet only if he partakes of an item that was permitted for consumption or for the altar by another item. As for the items listed here, either nothing else renders them permitted for consumption or for the altar, or they themselves render other items permitted. They are as follows:

chunks.en: the kometz, the levonah, the ketores, and the mincha of Kohanim,
chunks.st: The handful of flour, which permits consumption of the meal offering; the incense, which is burned in its entirety, without another item rendering it permitted for the altar; the frankincense, which is burned together with the handful of the meal offering; the meal offering of priests,
chunks.stMore: from which no handful of flour is removed and which is burned in its entirety (see Leviticus 6:16);

words.note: The handful of flour taken from a mincha and burned on the mizbeach.
The incense burned inside the Heichal.

chunks.en: the mincha of the Kohen Gadol, and the mincha of the nesachim,
chunks.st: the meal offering of the anointed priest,
chunks.stMore: which is sacrificed by the High Priest each day, half in the morning and half in the evening;

words.note: The Kohen Gadol, who was anointed with special oil.
Some texts do not have these words.

chunks.en: the blood, and the nesachim that come by themselves,
chunks.st: the blood, which permits all the offerings; and the libations that are brought by themselves
chunks.stMore: as a separate offering and do not accompany an animal offering;

chunks.en: says Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: even those that come with the animal korban.
chunks.st: The same halakha applies even with regard to libations that are brought with an animal offering.

chunks.en: The log of oil of a metzora,
chunks.st: With regard to the log of oil that accompanies the guilt offering of a recovered leper,

words.note: A measure, about a small cup.
A person who had tzaraas and became tahor.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: one is not punished for it because of piggul.
chunks.st: One is not liable for consuming it due to violation of the prohibition of piggul, because it is not permitted by any other item.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: And Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: one is punished for it because of piggul,
chunks.st: One is liable for consuming it due to violation of the prohibition of piggul,

chunks.en: because the blood of the asham makes it allowed.
chunks.st: as the blood of the guilt offering of the leper permits its
chunks.stMore: use, as only after the blood’s sacrifice is the oil sprinkled and given to the priests.

chunks.en: And anything that has something that makes it allowed,
chunks.st: And the principle is: With regard to any item that has permitting factors,

chunks.en: either for a person or for the mizbeach,
chunks.st: either for consumption by a person or for burning on the altar,

chunks.en: one is punished for it because of piggul.
chunks.st: one is liable for eating it due to violation of the prohibition of piggul.

summary: This mishnah tells what the blood of different korbanos makes allowed. Rabbi Shimon says a korban whose blood is not put on the outer mizbeach cannot become piggul.

chunks.en: The olah: its blood makes its meat allowed
chunks.st: The mishna elaborates: The burnt offering, its blood permits its flesh to

chunks.en: for the mizbeach, and its skin for the Kohanim.
chunks.st: be burned on the altar and its hide to be used by the priests.

chunks.en: A bird olah:
chunks.st: The bird burnt offering,

chunks.en: its blood makes its meat allowed for the mizbeach.
chunks.st: its blood permits its flesh and its skin to be burned on the altar.

chunks.en: A bird chatas:
chunks.st: The bird sin offering,

chunks.en: its blood makes its meat allowed for the Kohanim.
chunks.st: its blood permits its meat for consumption by the priests.

chunks.en: The bulls that are burned and the goats that are burned:
chunks.st: Bulls that are burned, e.g., the bull for an unwitting communal sin, and goats that are burned,
chunks.stMore: e.g., the goats sacrificed for an unwitting communal sin of idol worship,

words.note: Special korbanos burned outside Yerushalayim instead of being eaten.

chunks.en: their blood makes their parts allowed to be offered.
chunks.st: their blood permits their sacrificial portions to be sacrificed on the altar.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.stMore: Those bulls and goats are not subject to piggul because their blood is presented in the Sanctuary,

chunks.he: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ עַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן כִּשְׁלָמִים,
chunks.en: anything whose blood is not on the outer mizbeach like a shelamim,
chunks.st: and in the case of any offering whose blood is not presented on the external altar like that of a peace offering,
chunks.stMore: with regard to which the halakha of piggul was stated in the Torah,

chunks.en: one is not punished for it because of piggul.
chunks.st: one is not liable for eating it due to violation of the prohibition of piggul.

summary: Korbanos of non-Jews cannot become piggul, nosar or tamei. Things that cannot become piggul can still become nosar or tamei, except the blood; Rabbi Shimon says that applies only to food.

chunks.en: Korbanos of non-Jews,
chunks.st: With regard to offerings consecrated by gentiles for sacrifice to God,

chunks.en: one is not punished for them because of piggul,
chunks.st: one is not liable for eating them, neither due to violation of the prohibition of piggul
chunks.stMore: if the sacrificial rites were performed with the intent to eat the offering beyond its designated time,

chunks.en: nosar, or tumah.
chunks.st: nor due to violation of the prohibition of notar, nor due to violation of the prohibition against eating the meat while ritually impure.

chunks.en: And one who shechts them outside
chunks.st: And one who slaughters them outside

words.note: Outside the courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: is not punished, says Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: the Temple courtyard is exempt; this is the statement of Rabbi Shimon.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says he is punished.
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yosei deems him liable.

chunks.he: דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין חַיָּבִין עֲלֵיהֶם מִשּׁוּם פִּגּוּל,
chunks.en: Things for which one is not punished because of piggul,
chunks.st: Even with regard to those items enumerated in the previous mishna (42b) for which one is not liable for eating them due to violation of the prohibition of piggul, e.g., the handful, the frankincense, and the incense,

chunks.en: one is punished for them because of nosar
chunks.st: one is, nevertheless, liable for eating them due to violation of the prohibition of notar,

chunks.en: and because of tumah,
chunks.st: and due to violation of the prohibition against eating consecrated food while ritually impure,

chunks.en: except for the blood.
chunks.st: except for the blood.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon deems one liable

chunks.en: only for something that is usually eaten.
chunks.st: for an item whose typical manner is such that one eats it.

chunks.en: But things like the wood, the levonah, and the ketores,
chunks.st: But with regard to the wood, the frankincense, and the incense,

chunks.en: one is not punished for them because of tumah.
chunks.st: one is not liable for eating them due to violation of the prohibition against eating a consecrated item while ritually impure.

summary: A korban is shechted with six things in mind, like the kind of korban, its owner and Hashem. Rabbi Yosei says it is kosher even without thinking of them, because Beis Din made a rule not to say any thought at all.

chunks.en: A korban is shechted for the sake of six things:
chunks.st: The slaughtered offering is slaughtered for the sake of six matters, and one must have all of these matters in mind:

chunks.en: for the sake of the korban,
chunks.st: For the sake of the particular type of offering being sacrificed;

chunks.en: for the sake of the one who brings it,
chunks.st: for the sake of the one who sacrifices the offering;

chunks.en: for the sake of Hashem,
chunks.st: for the sake of God;

chunks.en: for the sake of the fires of the mizbeach,
chunks.st: for the sake of consumption by the fires of the altar;

chunks.en: for the sake of the smell,
chunks.st: for the sake of the aroma;

chunks.en: for the sake of being pleasing to Hashem.
chunks.st: for the sake of the pleasing of God, i.e., in fulfillment of God’s will;

chunks.en: And the chatas and the asham,
chunks.st: and, in the cases of a sin offering and a guilt offering,

chunks.en: for the sake of the sin.
chunks.st: for the sake of atonement for the sin.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: even one who did not have in mind
chunks.st: Even in the case of one who did not have in mind

chunks.en: any one of all these,
chunks.st: to slaughter the offering for the sake of any one of these,

chunks.en: it is kosher, because this is a rule of Beis Din,
chunks.st: the offering is valid, as it is a stipulation of the court that he should not state any intent ab initio.

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵין הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה הוֹלֶכֶת אֶלָּא אַחַר הָעוֹבֵד:
chunks.en: since a thought goes only after the one doing the avodah.
chunks.st: This is necessary because the intent follows only the one performing the sacrificial rite,
chunks.stMore: and therefore if the one who slaughters the animal is not careful and states the wrong intent, the offering would be disqualified through his improper intent.
